 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Chicago Blackhawks (6-13-2) conclude a four-game homestand against the Columbus Blue Jackets (7-12-0) at the United Center on Thursday. The game is scheduled for 7:00 p.m. CT and will be broadcast on CHSN.
 Thursday marks the first of two meetings between the Blackhawks and Blue Jackets in the 2026-27 season, with Nationwide Arena in Columbus hosting the series finale on Mar. 25, 2027.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Blackhawks are coming off a 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday, moving to 2-0-1 in the first three games of the homestand. Frank Nazar and Tyler Bertuzzi each scored twice, while Sam Rinzel added three assists. Connor Bedard and Oliver Moore also scored, and Spencer Knight stopped 31 of 34 shots.
 Unfortunately, Bedard suffered another right shoulder injury early in the third period, spoiling the three-goal win on the 100th anniversary of the franchise's first-ever game. Bedard and Leafs center Nick Paul were battling at the faceoff circle, and Paul's stick-lift appeared to jerk Bedard's shoulder in an awkward direction. The captain skated off the ice in visible discomfort and frustration, as it's his third shoulder injury in less than one year.
 Bedard's status remains to be determined, but the Blackhawks will be without their best player and top-line center against Columbus on Thursday.
 Like the Maple Leafs on Tuesday, the Blue Jackets enter the United Center in the midst of a losing skid, having dropped each of their last five games. Columbus has been outscored 21-8 and scored three goals in a single game only once during the losing streak.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Last time out, the Blue Jackets fell 5-1 on the road to the New York Islanders on Tuesday, with 2025 No. 1 overall pick Matthew Schaefer recording his first NHL hat trick. Zach Werenski's early third-period tally was the team's lone goal. Cam Talbot started in net and allowed four goals on 40 shots.
 Thursday's meeting is between two of the NHL's three worst offensive teams, with the Blackhawks ranked 30th in goals per game (2.48) and Columbus ranked 32nd (2.32). Both clubs are also tied for the second-fewest points in the league with 14, ahead of only the Vancouver Canucks.
 It's another bottom-feeder matchup at the United Center to close out the four-game homestand.
 Here's everything else to know before the puck drops at 7:00 p.m. CT in Chicago.

 ***
 The Blackhawks held an optional morning skate, so their official lineup is to be determined. The forward lines and defensive pairings listed above are from Wednesday's practice.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Rookie Anton Frondell is expected to replace Bedard as the team's top-line center between Roman Kantserov and Tyler Bertuzzi.
 Happy 38th Birthday to Patrick Kane! Where has the time gone?!! Kane is projected to skate on the second line with Frank Nazar and Oliver Moore. "Showtime" has recorded more points (91) and assists (62) against the Blue Jackets than any other opponent in his career.
 Ryan Greene has been moved up to third-line center between Cole Smith and Teuvo Teravainen . Smith did not practice on Wednesday but is expected to play against Columbus.
 Ryan Donato is now playing center on the fourth line instead of right wing, with Andrew Mangiapane and Dillon Boucher expected to be his linemates. Boucher was scratched for the last three games.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bowen Byram will miss his 15th straight game due to an upper-body injury. Byram participated in the morning skate, but continues to wear a grey non-contact sweater. It's TBD if he'll travel with the Blackhawks for the upcoming three-game road trip.

 Projected Goaltending Matchup
 Drew Commesso (0-0-0) vs. Cam Talbot (5-4-0, 2.67 GAA, .908 Sv%, 0 SO) 
 Commesso could make his first NHL start of the season for the Blackhawks. He's served as Spencer Knight's backup for three games since being recalled from Rockford on Nov. 8. Commesso is 2-2-0 with a 2.61 GAA, .901 Sv%, and 1 shutout in five career NHL appearances.
 Talbot will make his 10th start of the season for the Blue Jackets. In his last start on Tuesday, the 39-year-old veteran allowed four goals on 40 shots in a 5-1 loss to the Islanders. Talbot is 14-7-1 with a 2.14 GAA, .926 Sv%, and four shutouts in 22 career games against Chicago.
